name: GitHub
summary: Register a user-authorized OAuth App. If you need fine-grained repository permissions or app-owned automation, use the separate GitHub App setup path instead.
effort: 1–3 hours · planning estimate for a first test connection

name: Notion
summary: A public OAuth integration can connect users across workspaces. Marketplace listing is a separate, optional review.
effort: 2–4 hours · planning estimate for a first test connection

name: Slack
summary: Pilot across workspaces with OAuth; assess Marketplace suitability before planning commercial distribution.
effort: 3–6 hours · planning estimate for OAuth and a pilot checklist

name: Google / Gmail
summary: Your scopes determine the path. Sending mail is sensitive; reading a mailbox is restricted and can add a security assessment.
effort: 4–8 hours · planning estimate for setup and review preparation, excluding assessment

name: LinkedIn
summary: Product access comes before OAuth. Basic sign-in is self-service; many business APIs require explicit program approval.
effort: 2–4 hours · planning estimate for registration and an access application

name: Zoom
summary: Choose management and distribution separately. External beta and public distribution have approval requirements.
effort: 3–6 hours · planning estimate for OAuth and review preparation

name: Shopify
summary: Select distribution before investing in launch. Public apps require approval; custom distribution targets a limited merchant audience.
effort: 4–8 hours · planning estimate for a test installation and launch checklist

name: Atlassian
summary: Create one distributable 3LO integration. Enable sharing, map site access, and keep user permissions distinct from OAuth scopes.
effort: 2–5 hours · planning estimate for an initial Jira connection
